thread: Follow the rails from stations and signal boxes, through a yard of locomotives and carriages, and into a city aboard a tram. The swarm can become a semaphore, a wheel arrangement, or a trolley pole reaching for the wires.

candidates.name: Ferrovie Nord Virtual Museum
candidates.why: Start along a railway network of distinctive stations, vanished crossings, viaducts and workshops; interlocking levers and signals make a mechanical nervous system for the swarm.

candidates.name: National Railway Museum, Adelaide
candidates.why: Steam and diesel locomotives, royal carriages, freight vehicles, station equipment and signalling invite the swarm to assemble itself into an Australian train.

candidates.name: National Tramway Museum
candidates.why: Finish in the streets among horse-drawn, steam and electric tramcars, with restoration projects, photographs and online exhibitions full of details to borrow.

candidates.name: Melbourne Tram Museum
candidates.why: A heritage depot shelters toast-rack cars, experimental trams and the familiar W class; articles trace the tracks, equipment and streets around them.

candidates.name: Tramway Museum Society of Victoria
candidates.why: Cable and horse trams, work cars, motor vehicles and restoration projects offer spare parts and curious ancestors for a street-running swarm.

candidates.name: Ballarat Tramway Museum
candidates.why: Individual tram profiles, local tramway history and online exhibits show how vehicles were built, used and restored along a historic city route.

candidates.name: Sydney Tramway Museum
candidates.why: A fleet from Sydney and cities around the world offers many shapes of electric tram, along with overhead wires, depot work and preserved street equipment.

candidates.name: North Yorkshire Moors Railway
candidates.why: Historic stations, steam and diesel locomotives, wagons, signals and workshop practices provide another route through a working railway landscape.
